To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the growth of Cu6Sn5 is faster than that of Cu3Sn under constant power loading, (ii) the growth of the Cu3Sn layer at the anode side is faster than at the cathode side, (iii) the growth of both layers at the cathodic side is slower than at the anodic side, (iv) the growth of IMC layers under cyclic power loading depends on the on- and off-periods of the power load and the thermal cycling

the growth behavior of the interfacial IMCs can be rationalized by the intrinsic flux of each element, and that power cycling with alternating current and temperature is more detrimental for the growth of intermetallic compounds than steady-state current stressing.
the evolution of the IMC layers at the cathodic and anodic sides of the interconnection are governed by different processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of constant and cyclic currents on the evolution of IMC layers in lead-free interconnections.
the effect of current stressing on the growth of intermetallic compounds in the Cu-SN system, with special focus on the evolution of the interfacial reaction layer at the solder/Cu6Sn5 interface.
the understanding of electromigration-induced changes in the growth kinetics of the IMC layers in lead-free solders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of electron current on the growth of IMC layers in the Cu-Su system is not as simple as it was thought to be before.
the growth rate of Cu3Sn at the cathode is higher than that of Cu6Sn5, whereas the growth rate of the Cu3Sn at anode is slower than that of Cu3Sn5.
the growth of the IMCs in the Cu-Su system can be controlled and tailored by the application of a current density and a power cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it is possible to obtain a steady-state IMC layer thickness evolution under power cycling conditions, but only if the temperature is chosen in such a manner that no melting of the interconnections is observed.
the growth of the Cu-Sn IMC layers is strongly dependent on the electron flux.
the effect of current on the growth of interfacial IMC layers is not a simple one.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the growth of IMC layers is not only dependent on the applied current density, but also on the temperature and the current cycle time (i.e., the time during which the current flows in a given direction).
the effect of electron flow on the evolution of reaction layers is more complex than previously thought.
the growth kinetics of interfacial layers can be significantly affected by current stressing, but that the effect of current stressing is not the same as for power cycling.
